seed.name: predisposition to invasive fungal disease due to CARD9 deficiency

partners.mechanism_chain: CARD9 (HGNC:13209) —DISRUPTS→ Downstream CARD9 signaling (GO:0038096); Downstream CARD9 signaling (GO:0038096) —LEADS_TO→ Invasive fungal disease (HP:0011091); IKBKG (HGNC:5870) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP512); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP512) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001052); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP512) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). Deficiency in CARD9 impairs signaling downstream of C-type lectin receptors, leading to invasive fungal disease. Deficiency in IKBKG (NEMO), a crucial component of the IKK complex, disrupts the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, resulting in ectodermal dysplasia and immunodeficiency. Both CARD9 signaling and the broader NF-kappaB pathway are critical for immune responses, and their disruption leads to distinct but related clinical phenotypes.

partners.diseaseBName: severe combined immunodeficiency due to IKK2 deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: CARD9 (HGNC:14747) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB activation downstream of CARD9 (GO:0043122); NF-kappaB activation downstream of CARD9 (GO:0043122) —DECREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP43); IKK2 (IKBKB) (HGNC:5924) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB activation by IKK complex (GO:0043122); NF-kappaB activation by IKK complex (GO:0043122) —DECREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP43); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP43) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired immune response (HP:0002715); Impaired immune response (HP:0002715) —LEADS_TO→ Predisposition to invasive fungal disease (HP:0011397). Loss-of-function mutations in CARD9 impair downstream NF-kappaB activation in response to fungal PAMPs, leading to reduced immune responses and susceptibility to invasive fungal infections. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in IKK2 (a key component of the IKK complex) directly disrupt the canonical NF-kappaB activation pathway, resulting in a severe combined immunodeficiency that can manifest as increased susceptibility to infections, including fungal pathogens.

Deficiency in CARD9 impairs signaling downstream of C-type lectin receptors, leading to invasive fungal disease. Deficiency in IKBKG (NEMO), a crucial component of the IKK complex, disrupts the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, resulting in ectodermal dysplasia and immunodeficiency. Both CARD9 signaling and the broader NF-kappaB pathway are critical for immune responses, and their disruption leads to distinct but related clinical phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that CARD9 and IKBKG do not functionally converge at any point in the upstream or downstream signaling cascades relevant to immune cell activation and cytokine production, or identification of mutations in CARD9 or IKBKG with a demonstrable gain-of-function effect in either disease. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in HGNC:13209 or HGNC:5870 in diverse populations that do not result in these phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the overlap in immune signaling pathways disrupted by CARD9 and IKBKG deficiencies could reveal common therapeutic targets for managing infections in immunodeficient patients or for modulating immune responses in related inflammatory conditions. Targeting the NF-kappaB pathway or its downstream effectors might offer a common therapeutic strategy.
